The VBS Eight Unmasked

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Eight men have been arrested for masterminding one of South Africa’s biggest bank heists, a theft in excess of 2 billion rand. Where did the money go and who will be next?

Unique Selling Point:
Eight kingpins have been arrested for the Great VBS Mutual Bank robbery in 2018, totaling an excess of 2.3 billion Rand. Who were they and how did they manage to almost pull off a masterminded Ponzi scheme doomed to fail. In advocate Terry Motau’s report The Great Bank Heist, 53 individuals were identified as being part of the operation. So which heads are going to roll next? Politicians, businessmen and corrupt municipal officials are implicated in Motau’s report.
Will we get clarity on the supposed ‘hits’ resulting in the death of two union representatives opposed to the looting? Their families speak out.
We follow the money and try to make sense of it all through forensic accountant Andre Prakke and liquidator Anush Rooplal.

Summary:
Two years have passed since the collapse and liquidation of Venda Building Society (VBS) Mutual Bank as a result of one of the most daring bank robberies in South African history. The robbers were the bank’s own executives and cronies solicited from businesses and municipalities to execute the theft of over 2 billion rand.
In Advocate Terry Motau’s report The Great Bank Heist to the Prudential Authority, 53 colluders and conspirators were identified and now eight, which includes the chairperson of VBS Mutual Bank, Tshifhiwa Matodzi, have been arrested. Who are these men and how did they pull it off? Many people lost their life savings and the poorest of the poor were the victims.


The accused:

1. Former VBS Mutual Bank and Vele Investments chairman Tshifhiwa Calvin Matodzi;
2. Former VBS Mutual Bank CEO Andile Ramavhunga
3. Former VBS CFO Philip Truter
4. Former VBS treasurer Phophi Mukhodobwane
5. Former KPMG partner Sipho Malaba
6. Former SAPS CFO Avashoni Ramikosi
7. Former Public Investment Corporation executive Ernest Nesane
8. Former Public Investment Corporation executive Paul Magula.

Further information:
The state has lined up 42 witnesses against the accused. VBS Mutual Bank's financial statements: 'Cooked, false and flawed' - the VBS financial statements painted a rosy picture while the bank was in actual fact insolvent.
The court granted all eight accused bail of R100,000 each, and the matter was postponed to October.
In a police investigation lead by the Hawks over fifty personnel were tasked to close in on the operation. This is the first leg of the arrests and in the second leg, will involve the arrest of politicians, businesses, municipalities and individuals that participated in the looting according to the Hawks.
Political leaders from the EFF like Julius Malema and Floyd Shivambu have been implicated, although they deny any wrongdoing in a released statement.
Provincial Treasurer for the ANC in Limpopo, Danny Msiza is also implicated in the soliciting of Municipal Deposits that bolstered the bank’s books. Twenty municipalities deposited a total of 1.5 billion rand which went straight into the pockets of the “robbers” and their cronies.
Our story tracks some of the municipal officials who lost their lives and whose lives were threatened because of their resistance to the VBS deposits.
Forensic Accountant, Danny Prakke and liquidator Anush Rooplal, examine the scale of the theft and follow the money.
This is just the beginning of the round-up of the VBS thieves, unveiling the web of corruption and looting of VBS Mutual Bank.

The South African Municipal Workers’ Union (Samwu) was devastated after the death of its Limpopo deputy secretary Ronald Mani, who was shot and killed at his home village of Tshisahulu outside Thohoyandou."His shooting came days after the attempted assassination of Timson "TT" Tshililo, also an employee of the Vhembe District Municipality and former Samwu Limpopo chairperson. Tshililo was rushed to hospital but succumbed to his injuries.
"We are definitely convinced that the two shootings are related as both victims are employees of the municipality and have been in the forefront of protests which led to the removal of mayors who illegally invested money with the now liquidated VBS Mutual Bank," Mathe said.
Case studies: Killed Whistleblowers:
Ronald Mani:
Deputy Provincial Secretary:
Preceding the South African Reserve Bank’s report on the VBS, increasing violence led to the death of union reps, part of the Municipal Workers Union, who were at the forefront of protests which led to the removal of Mayors who illegally invested municipal money into VBS. VBS came to prominence in 2016 when it granted a R7.8 million loan to former president Jacob Zuma to settle debt relating to the upgrades to his Nkandla home. Despite the Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA) forbidding municipalities to invest with mutual banks, many did. In early 2017, Treasury issued an instruction to municipalities to stop investing with the institution.
As a result, a number of councils withdrew more than R1 billion from the bank.

The victims of the shootings were Ronald Mani and Tshililo Timson Musetsho.

Ronald Mani Was killed in January 2019 at his Home village in Tshisahulu outside Thohoyandou, after attending a general meeting in the Vhembe District. He was one of the few that were vocal about the looting of the bank from which over R 2,3 Billion was stolen. Their killings have been linked to the VBS looting as days before he and some of his colleagues had been addressing municipal workers about the looting.

The Vhembe District Municipality had invested 311 Million into VBS Mutual Bank In contravention of the regulations.

He was one of the leaders from the Union Federation Cosatu and the South african Communist party acting in various capacities at local and regional levels, until his election as deputy secretary in 2016 of the South African Municipal Workers Union.

His wife is still mourning the death of her husband, particularly as no suspects, have been arrested. Her Son has said that his mother gets epileptic fits when she speaks about his death.

Tshililo Timson Musetsho:

Another ‘Comrade’, Tshililo Timson Musetsho, was killed before Ronald Mani. TT was rushed to the hospital where he later died. At the bail appearance of the VBS Eight Accused, Timson’s daughter wrote on twitter,

“My father was brutally killed Last year because he stood up for the people and fought against VBS Looters, let you politician friend that they are also coming for them, they gonna rot in jail, my father's death will never be in vain RIP Cd TT, God is Fighting for u. # VBSArrests #VBSBankhiest.

Lucky Mani, brother of Ronald Mani, has agreed to speak to Carte Blanche regarding the movement of the case. The brother of the deceased says that Ronald had been vocal long before the report was released. This intensified and they placed pressure on the municipality to stop with the illegal investments. He says that even though there is progress with the arrests of the VBS accused, nothing will make the family find solace if the killers of Mani and TT are not found.

Lucky Mani says that because the death of his brother received a lot of attention in Vhembe, a group of ANC officials, union reps etc. have been helping to put pressure on the police to find the killers - It's a wait and see game for them.

Case Number Sourced:
481/10/2018
Sergeant SB Libanyana
Contact: 013 980 0048

South African National Civic Organisation SANCO National: SANCO:
SANCO, has been representing individuals in the community most affected by the VBS Heist. They are creating a database of individuals who have lost money and are planning to demand that the government give those individuals monthly relief fund packages from the 500 Billion COVID- Relief fund, to help those who lost all their savings.

NOTE: According to Mosibudi, while in Vhembe we will be able to speak to specific individuals, who lost 100k or more.: we will be able to have one or two other interviews, regarding the loss of funds through VBS and what future plans SANCO, have, to help the affected individuals.

Extra Budget Items:
The Accused:

Accused number 1: Tshifhiwa Matodzi, former chairman VBS
The indictment shows that Matodzi had control of several accounts held at VBS Mutual Bank. The accounts included: Vele investments, Petronet, Venmont, Robvet, Khavo, Scorpion, Tiisang. These accounts controlled hundreds of millions of rand, some of which Matodzi used to bribe his co-accused, prosecutors allege.
Prosecutors also accused Matodzi of offering gratification in order to influence them “to act in a manner that amounts to the illegal, dishonest, unauthorised, incomplete, or biased exercise, carrying out or performance of any powers, duties or functions arising out of a statutory, contractual or any other legal obligation”.

Accused Number 2: Andile Ramavhunga, former CEO VBS
Between December 2016 and February 2018, the indictment shows, Ramavhunga received about R19m into the account of “Dambale”, a company owned by him. Other accounts, held at VBS Mutual Bank, which Ramavhunga controlled, include those of Munyai Investments and another one named in the indictment as the “Ramavhunga” account.
Ramavhunga received R3.7m into the Munyai Investments account. The money came from the Vele and Vele Petroport accounts, the indictment shows. Also, he received R795,000 into the Ramavhunga account from the Venmont, Vele and Petroport accounts. Up to February 2018, Ramavhunga’s accounts had received a total of R23.4m.

Accused number 3: Philip Truter, former CFO VBS
The indictment shows that Truter received R2m into the FNB account of a company called Shangri La Investments.

Accused number 4: Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer VBS
On the instruction of Matodzi, Mukhodobwane received R5.6m into the account of Lamawave Ltd. The indictment shows that a Peter Mukhodobwane, who was the sole shareholder of Lamawave, was a front for Phophi Mukhodobwane, the former treasurer. In total, Mukhodobwane received R17.1m into Lamawave and the “Mukhodobwane” accounts.

Accused number 5: Sipho Malaba, former KPMG partner
Malaba has been charged with fraud for signing off VBS Bank’s 2017 financial statements which gave the false impression that its finances were in a healthy state.
Malaba, Matodzi, Ramavhunga, Truter, Nesane and Magula were also collectively charged with “unlawfully, falsely and with the intention to defraud ... shareholders, VBS creditors and the Registrar” approving the financial statements.”
On the money trail against Malaba, the indictment shows that a company called Ihaawu Lesizwe, owned by Jacqueline Jaseman Malaba and Bafana Milundelwa Malaba, had the following accounts at VBS Mutual Bank: two vehicle finance accounts, a mortgage account and a classic business account.
Betanologix, another company owned by Jacqueline Jaseman Malaba and a Mwise Mapepo, also had an account at the bank. Up to March 2018 both companies, which the indictment claims were fronts for Sipho Malaba, received up to R29.2m.
Further, on Matodzi’s instruction, R654,000 was paid into the trust accounts of Makaula Zilwa Inc and NGL attorneys on behalf of Malaba.

Accused number 6: Avashoni Ramikosi, former police CFO.
The indictment shows that a company called Zanoware, owned by Alice Manye, was a front for Ramikosi. The company had received up to R750,000 from Venmont, one of the many accounts controlled by Matodzi.

Accused number 7: Ernest Nesane, former PIC executive
Nesane, the prosecutors will argue, received up to R1.1m into the account of a company called Parallel Properties owned by Rudzani Ndwammbi. Ndwammbi, prosecutors will argue, was a front for Nesane, as all monies received by Parallel Properties benefited the former PIC executive. Also, on the instruction of Matodzi, prosecutors revealed that Nesane benefited from R5.6m which was paid into Parallel Properties from the Vele account.

Accused number 8: Paul Magula, former PIC executive
The indictment shows that a company called Investar Connect Holdings, owned by a Lot Magosha, was a front for Magula.The company was paid R2.8m for the benefit of Magula on instruction from Matodzi.Another company, Hekima Capital, which had an account at VBS Mutual Bank, received R3.3m on behalf of Magula on Matodzi’s instruction.

In addition we received an email from the family of a deceased 24 year old, Dylan Ross who was killed in a car accident on the 24th of August 2019. They allege that it was reckelss driving by Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer of VBS, who fled the scene of the accident and only later report it, as well as have sms communication with the family that he felt really bad about what happened that night. They have laid a charge of reckless driving but nothing has come of the case as yet, it may be worth a one line mention...
One other element which I am keen on, is that in the last 14 years only 67 municipal people have been charged with corruption of which only 9 have been convicted with sentences of 2 to 3 years and wholly suspended for 5 years. I would like the NPA to answer to; if municipal officials are charged in this case, what kind of sentences could they expect bearing in mind the nature of the crimes.

Press Release:


An investigation that took almost two years to complete has finally brought the alleged looters of VBS Mutual Bank to court. What more will this hive of corruption reveal?

Script:


VO: Two years have passed since the collapse and then liquidation of VBS Mutual Bank.
// (beat: shot of VBS Bank closed)
The consequence of one of the most brazen bank heists in South African history. A reported 2.3 billion rand was looted. //
VO: Anoosh Rooplal, Curator and Liquidator of VBS Mutual Bank, appointed by the Prudential Authority.

Anoosh: This was a Ponzi scheme, criminal enterprise. And it certainly was a fraudulent scheme.

VO: In a forensic report conducted in 2018 by Advocate Terry Motau on behalf of the Prudential Authority, the scale of the theft was uncovered, allegedly implicating some of the banks top brass in a widespread web of collusion. Depositors' money, many of which were stokvels and burial societies amongst others, was siphoned out of the bank in order to enrich the network of looters.
Sipho: This is a huge criminal activity. 2.3 billion is not child's play.

VO: Sipho Ngwema - spokesperson for the National Prosecuting Authority.

Sipho: This affects the poor people of Limpopo and beyond. You would see those people sitting in the pavement, crying over their last pennies that they would have invested in this particular bank.

General: Nobody could have received a cent unless it was sanctioned from the bank itself. They have enabled others to be able to get the funds

(intro shot - track around if there is slow mo)

VO: Lt General Godfrey Lebeya - Head of the Hawks

General: Those who were in leadership positions need to go and prove their innocence at court.


VO: Finally, eight alleged kingpins behind the VBS Mutual Bank Heist were arrested and seven appeared in the Specialised Commercial Crimes Court in Johannesburg on the 18th of June for their bail hearing. The eight are charged with a total of 47 counts related to the plundering of the bank's assets, including racketeering,// fraud,// theft,//corruption// and money laundering. All eight accused are charged with being complicit in the theft of almost R 2.3bn from VBS. //
All seven who appeared in court pleaded not guilty and made Bail of 100 thousand rands each.

Link: So who are they? and how did they almost manage to pull it off?

VO: Accused 1: Tshifhiwa Matodzi, former VBS director and chairman of the board.

VO: According to the State's Indictment, Matodzi, along with Accused 2 Andile Ramavhunga Former VBS CEO, Accused 3 Philip Truter Former CFO of VBS and Accused 4 Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer of VBS created fictitious credits in the VBS accounts of companies of which they and their associates were beneficiaries.
[build of first 4 accused ]
In addition, allegedly on Matodzi’s instructions payments were made from VBS accounts of Matodzi entities to VBS accounts of front companies linked to all the accused.
[build up to all the accused ]
Whilst Matodzi was chairman of VBS he was also executive Chairman of Vele Investments which had acquired a questionable 53% shareholding in VBS.

Anoosh: Vele was part and parcel of the entire scheme. So it became essentially the alter ego of the bank. Where monies were siphoned out and diverted through to Vele; Vele would then use those funds to buy up other companies and further utilize those monies for other purposes.

VO: The questionable acquisition of Vele's shares in VBS forms part of Matodzi's charge sheet and is linked to the charges of Accused 7 Ernest Nesane and Accused 8 Paul Magula who were non-executive directors of VBS and represented the PIC's 26% interest in VBS Mutual Bank.

Anoosh: Things just weren't tying up. Essentially, when one tried to trace and understand where the assets of the bank were, you know, we found that they were really weak cases of assets and cash that were reflected on the records.

Anoosh: Every bank has to have third party assurance providers. The auditors are one of them. I had to withdraw those financial statements purely because they were unreliable.

VO: Accused 6: Avashoni Ramikosi, former Chairman of the VBS Audit Committee and SAPS Chief Financial Officer, Was Allegedly instrumental in approving the fraudulent VBS 2017 financials. The indictment shows payments of R 750 000 to Ramikosi.

VO: Forensic Accountant Andre Prakke examined the Motau Report and the indictment and explains why he thinks the alleged looters managed to carry on for as long as they did.

Andre: By the assistance of the auditor.

VO: The auditor being, former KPMG partner Sipho Malaba

Andre: This is a very good example where the head of the audit committee was fed information, and they knew it was not correct and it was manipulated before it went to the audit committee. It's clear from the report also that even the CFO and the directors knew things were false. The whole idea of this was to steal the money and then you forge and change and the auditor was the key person to achieve this.

VO: KPMG have stated they have "fully cooperated with the Reserve Bank" … and "Any unlawful action taken by Malaba, was neither authorised nor known to KPMG".

In response to our questions to all the accused, five responded. Malaba, Ramavhunga and Magula have denied any wrongdoing and intend to clear their names. Matodzi and Ramikosi are not prepared to comment at this stage.

Sipho: The people that have appeared in court right now, is the chairperson of the board, is the CEO of the company and his executives. So that's where you start, and then it trickles down. You follow the money in terms of how it filters through to everybody, and that's, the the strategy of the investigation

Link: Twenty municipalities were involved in this fraud, by illegally depositing a collective of 1.5 billion rand with VBS.

VO: To keep this pyramid scheme alive, the accused allegedly had to solicit big investors like Municipalities, in order to have money in the bank, so they could siphon it out.

Anoosh: One of the reasons that led to the curatorship was because municipalities were not legally allowed to invest the monies with the mutual bank in the first place.

VO: Some municipalities did pull their money out of VBS, but others were resistant, like the Vhembe District Municipality even with mounting pressure from unions.
The burning question in Vhembe today is, did some union members pay the ultimate price for their objections?

Musetsho wife: It was on the 24th of January, I was cooking in the kitchen when my son come running saying mama come help daddy, and I just felt a bang, I didn't realise it’s a gun.

VO: Tshililo Timson Musetsho known as TT, former Limpopo Chairperson of the South African Municipal Workers Union and Vhembe Municipality employee was gunned down at his home. The pain of losing her husband is unbearable for Luvhuenga Musetsho.

Musetsho Sound up: Eish, I don't want to talk about it

VO: TT's mother Agnes was with him before he passed away.

Venda: Agnes: I am hurting so much, what hurts more about this VBS issue is that at the end of the day I saw him shot. He said to me Ma VBS got me, today VBS has finally got me. I am dying because of VBS.

VO: Lucky Mani, describes how his brother Ronald Mani, Deputy Provincial Secretary of SAMWU, was shot at a friends shop a few days later.

Lucky: There were two people that walk into the shop, and ask for the owner of the shop and then they also ask for him and from there they move around the shop and then they then shot him.

VO: Both men stood against corruption in the Vhembe District Municipality which had illegally invested 300 million rand in VBS contravening the Municipal Finance Management Act. Subsequently, the Municipal Manager and the CFO were both subjected to a disciplinary process by the municipality. Pastor Dr Farisani Tshenuwani had attended a meeting involving various unions with Ronald on the day he died.

Pastor: Millions were given to identified people who were willing to work with the systems some politicians in the municipalities were getting kickbacks from the monies that were being invested in the VBS. They were demanding the removal of key players in the municipalities who were promoting the rot.

VO: According to the Motau report Municipal officials and middlemen were offered commissions of around 2% to deposit millions into VBS. // The Mani and Musetsho families firmly believe that the killings were linked to the VBS travesty. // A suspect in the death of Mani has been arrested.
Lucky: They might have killed him, but they didn't silence his voice.

VO: No arrests have yet been made in connection with TT's killing.

Masa: We have two union reps who were killed and their families alleged this is because they were quite outspoken about what was going on at VBS.
Sipho: We will make sure that we reveal or we extract any piece of evidence that suggests there were also other crimes that were committed like murder, connected to the VBS Bank.

VO: Not even a week after the arrest of the alleged Kingpins the Hawks pounced again, this time targeting municipalities making one arrest.

Link: In advocate Terry Motau's report, TheGreat Bank Heist , 53 conspirators were identified as being part of this elaborate operation, so who's next? Politicians, businessmen, corrupt municipal officials, are all implicated in Motau's report.

Sipho: Anyone who has committed criminal offences with this particular matter, If I were them, I wouldn't rest. It's just a matter of time.

Summary: Two years have passed since the collapse and liquidation of Venda Building Society (VBS) Mutual Bank as a result of one of the most daring bank robberies in South African history. The robbers were the bank’s own executives and cronies solicited from businesses and municipalities to execute the theft of over 2 billion rand. In Advocate Terry Motau’s report The Great Bank Heist to the Prudential Authority, 53 colluders and conspirators were identified and now eight, which includes the chairperson of VBS Mutual Bank, Tshifhiwa Matodzi, have been arrested. Who are these men and how did they pull it off? Many people lost their life savings and the poorest of the poor were the victims. The accused: 1. Former VBS Mutual Bank and Vele Investments chairman Tshifhiwa Calvin Matodzi; 2. Former VBS Mutual Bank CEO Andile Ramavhunga 3. Former VBS CFO Philip Truter 4. Former VBS treasurer Phophi Mukhodobwane 5. Former KPMG partner Sipho Malaba 6. Former SAPS CFO Avashoni Ramikosi 7. Former Public Investment Corporation executive Ernest Nesane 8. Former Public Investment Corporation executive Paul Magula. Further information: The state has lined up 42 witnesses against the accused. VBS Mutual Bank's financial statements: 'Cooked, false and flawed' - the VBS financial statements painted a rosy picture while the bank was in actual fact insolvent. The court granted all eight accused bail of R100,000 each, and the matter was postponed to October. In a police investigation lead by the Hawks over fifty personnel were tasked to close in on the operation. This is the first leg of the arrests and in the second leg, will involve the arrest of politicians, businesses, municipalities and individuals that participated in the looting according to the Hawks. Political leaders from the EFF like Julius Malema and Floyd Shivambu have been implicated, although they deny any wrongdoing in a released statement. Provincial Treasurer for the ANC in Limpopo, Danny Msiza is also implicated in the soliciting of Municipal Deposits that bolstered the bank’s books. Twenty municipalities deposited a total of 1.5 billion rand which went straight into the pockets of the “robbers” and their cronies. Our story tracks some of the municipal officials who lost their lives and whose lives were threatened because of their resistance to the VBS deposits. Forensic Accountant, Danny Prakke and liquidator Anush Rooplal, examine the scale of the theft and follow the money. This is just the beginning of the round-up of the VBS thieves, unveiling the web of corruption and looting of VBS Mutual Bank. The South African Municipal Workers’ Union (Samwu) was devastated after the death of its Limpopo deputy secretary Ronald Mani, who was shot and killed at his home village of Tshisahulu outside Thohoyandou."His shooting came days after the attempted assassination of Timson "TT" Tshililo, also an employee of the Vhembe District Municipality and former Samwu Limpopo chairperson. Tshililo was rushed to hospital but succumbed to his injuries. "We are definitely convinced that the two shootings are related as both victims are employees of the municipality and have been in the forefront of protests which led to the removal of mayors who illegally invested money with the now liquidated VBS Mutual Bank," Mathe said. Case studies: Killed Whistleblowers: Ronald Mani: Deputy Provincial Secretary: Preceding the South African Reserve Bank’s report on the VBS, increasing violence led to the death of union reps, part of the Municipal Workers Union, who were at the forefront of protests which led to the removal of Mayors who illegally invested municipal money into VBS. VBS came to prominence in 2016 when it granted a R7.8 million loan to former president Jacob Zuma to settle debt relating to the upgrades to his Nkandla home. Despite the Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA) forbidding municipalities to invest with mutual banks, many did. In early 2017, Treasury issued an instruction to municipalities to stop investing with the institution. As a result, a number of councils withdrew more than R1 billion from the bank. The victims of the shootings were Ronald Mani and Tshililo Timson Musetsho. Ronald Mani Was killed in January 2019 at his Home village in Tshisahulu outside Thohoyandou, after attending a general meeting in the Vhembe District. He was one of the few that were vocal about the looting of the bank from which over R 2,3 Billion was stolen. Their killings have been linked to the VBS looting as days before he and some of his colleagues had been addressing municipal workers about the looting. The Vhembe District Municipality had invested 311 Million into VBS Mutual Bank In contravention of the regulations. He was one of the leaders from the Union Federation Cosatu and the South african Communist party acting in various capacities at local and regional levels, until his election as deputy secretary in 2016 of the South African Municipal Workers Union. His wife is still mourning the death of her husband, particularly as no suspects, have been arrested. Her Son has said that his mother gets epileptic fits when she speaks about his death. Tshililo Timson Musetsho: Another ‘Comrade’, Tshililo Timson Musetsho, was killed before Ronald Mani. TT was rushed to the hospital where he later died. At the bail appearance of the VBS Eight Accused, Timson’s daughter wrote on twitter, “My father was brutally killed Last year because he stood up for the people and fought against VBS Looters, let you politician friend that they are also coming for them, they gonna rot in jail, my father's death will never be in vain RIP Cd TT, God is Fighting for u. # VBSArrests #VBSBankhiest. Lucky Mani, brother of Ronald Mani, has agreed to speak to Carte Blanche regarding the movement of the case. The brother of the deceased says that Ronald had been vocal long before the report was released. This intensified and they placed pressure on the municipality to stop with the illegal investments. He says that even though there is progress with the arrests of the VBS accused, nothing will make the family find solace if the killers of Mani and TT are not found. Lucky Mani says that because the death of his brother received a lot of attention in Vhembe, a group of ANC officials, union reps etc. have been helping to put pressure on the police to find the killers - It's a wait and see game for them. Case Number Sourced: 481/10/2018 Sergeant SB Libanyana Contact: 013 980 0048 South African National Civic Organisation SANCO National: SANCO: SANCO, has been representing individuals in the community most affected by the VBS Heist. They are creating a database of individuals who have lost money and are planning to demand that the government give those individuals monthly relief fund packages from the 500 Billion COVID- Relief fund, to help those who lost all their savings. NOTE: According to Mosibudi, while in Vhembe we will be able to speak to specific individuals, who lost 100k or more.: we will be able to have one or two other interviews, regarding the loss of funds through VBS and what future plans SANCO, have, to help the affected individuals. Extra Budget Items: The Accused: Accused number 1: Tshifhiwa Matodzi, former chairman VBS The indictment shows that Matodzi had control of several accounts held at VBS Mutual Bank. The accounts included: Vele investments, Petronet, Venmont, Robvet, Khavo, Scorpion, Tiisang. These accounts controlled hundreds of millions of rand, some of which Matodzi used to bribe his co-accused, prosecutors allege. Prosecutors also accused Matodzi of offering gratification in order to influence them “to act in a manner that amounts to the illegal, dishonest, unauthorised, incomplete, or biased exercise, carrying out or performance of any powers, duties or functions arising out of a statutory, contractual or any other legal obligation”. Accused Number 2: Andile Ramavhunga, former CEO VBS Between December 2016 and February 2018, the indictment shows, Ramavhunga received about R19m into the account of “Dambale”, a company owned by him. Other accounts, held at VBS Mutual Bank, which Ramavhunga controlled, include those of Munyai Investments and another one named in the indictment as the “Ramavhunga” account. Ramavhunga received R3.7m into the Munyai Investments account. The money came from the Vele and Vele Petroport accounts, the indictment shows. Also, he received R795,000 into the Ramavhunga account from the Venmont, Vele and Petroport accounts. Up to February 2018, Ramavhunga’s accounts had received a total of R23.4m. Accused number 3: Philip Truter, former CFO VBS The indictment shows that Truter received R2m into the FNB account of a company called Shangri La Investments. Accused number 4: Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer VBS On the instruction of Matodzi, Mukhodobwane received R5.6m into the account of Lamawave Ltd. The indictment shows that a Peter Mukhodobwane, who was the sole shareholder of Lamawave, was a front for Phophi Mukhodobwane, the former treasurer. In total, Mukhodobwane received R17.1m into Lamawave and the “Mukhodobwane” accounts. Accused number 5: Sipho Malaba, former KPMG partner Malaba has been charged with fraud for signing off VBS Bank’s 2017 financial statements which gave the false impression that its finances were in a healthy state. Malaba, Matodzi, Ramavhunga, Truter, Nesane and Magula were also collectively charged with “unlawfully, falsely and with the intention to defraud ... shareholders, VBS creditors and the Registrar” approving the financial statements.” On the money trail against Malaba, the indictment shows that a company called Ihaawu Lesizwe, owned by Jacqueline Jaseman Malaba and Bafana Milundelwa Malaba, had the following accounts at VBS Mutual Bank: two vehicle finance accounts, a mortgage account and a classic business account. Betanologix, another company owned by Jacqueline Jaseman Malaba and a Mwise Mapepo, also had an account at the bank. Up to March 2018 both companies, which the indictment claims were fronts for Sipho Malaba, received up to R29.2m. Further, on Matodzi’s instruction, R654,000 was paid into the trust accounts of Makaula Zilwa Inc and NGL attorneys on behalf of Malaba. Accused number 6: Avashoni Ramikosi, former police CFO. The indictment shows that a company called Zanoware, owned by Alice Manye, was a front for Ramikosi. The company had received up to R750,000 from Venmont, one of the many accounts controlled by Matodzi. Accused number 7: Ernest Nesane, former PIC executive Nesane, the prosecutors will argue, received up to R1.1m into the account of a company called Parallel Properties owned by Rudzani Ndwammbi. Ndwammbi, prosecutors will argue, was a front for Nesane, as all monies received by Parallel Properties benefited the former PIC executive. Also, on the instruction of Matodzi, prosecutors revealed that Nesane benefited from R5.6m which was paid into Parallel Properties from the Vele account. Accused number 8: Paul Magula, former PIC executive The indictment shows that a company called Investar Connect Holdings, owned by a Lot Magosha, was a front for Magula.The company was paid R2.8m for the benefit of Magula on instruction from Matodzi.Another company, Hekima Capital, which had an account at VBS Mutual Bank, received R3.3m on behalf of Magula on Matodzi’s instruction. In addition we received an email from the family of a deceased 24 year old, Dylan Ross who was killed in a car accident on the 24th of August 2019. They allege that it was reckelss driving by Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer of VBS, who fled the scene of the accident and only later report it, as well as have sms communication with the family that he felt really bad about what happened that night. They have laid a charge of reckless driving but nothing has come of the case as yet, it may be worth a one line mention... One other element which I am keen on, is that in the last 14 years only 67 municipal people have been charged with corruption of which only 9 have been convicted with sentences of 2 to 3 years and wholly suspended for 5 years. I would like the NPA to answer to; if municipal officials are charged in this case, what kind of sentences could they expect bearing in mind the nature of the crimes. in Show: Title Author Last Updated 05 July 2020 - Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 16 September 2020 Press Release: An investigation that took almost two years to complete has finally brought the alleged looters of VBS Mutual Bank to court. What more will this hive of corruption reveal? Script: VO: Two years have passed since the collapse and then liquidation of VBS Mutual Bank. // (beat: shot of VBS Bank closed) The consequence of one of the most brazen bank heists in South African history. A reported 2.3 billion rand was looted. // VO: Anoosh Rooplal, Curator and Liquidator of VBS Mutual Bank, appointed by the Prudential Authority. Anoosh: This was a Ponzi scheme, criminal enterprise. And it certainly was a fraudulent scheme. VO: In a forensic report conducted in 2018 by Advocate Terry Motau on behalf of the Prudential Authority, the scale of the theft was uncovered, allegedly implicating some of the banks top brass in a widespread web of collusion. Depositors' money, many of which were stokvels and burial societies amongst others, was siphoned out of the bank in order to enrich the network of looters. Sipho: This is a huge criminal activity. 2.3 billion is not child's play. VO: Sipho Ngwema - spokesperson for the National Prosecuting Authority. Sipho: This affects the poor people of Limpopo and beyond. You would see those people sitting in the pavement, crying over their last pennies that they would have invested in this particular bank. General: Nobody could have received a cent unless it was sanctioned from the bank itself. They have enabled others to be able to get the funds (intro shot - track around if there is slow mo) VO: Lt General Godfrey Lebeya - Head of the Hawks General: Those who were in leadership positions need to go and prove their innocence at court. VO: Finally, eight alleged kingpins behind the VBS Mutual Bank Heist were arrested and seven appeared in the Specialised Commercial Crimes Court in Johannesburg on the 18th of June for their bail hearing. The eight are charged with a total of 47 counts related to the plundering of the bank's assets, including racketeering,// fraud,// theft,//corruption// and money laundering. All eight accused are charged with being complicit in the theft of almost R 2.3bn from VBS. // All seven who appeared in court pleaded not guilty and made Bail of 100 thousand rands each. Link: So who are they? and how did they almost manage to pull it off? VO: Accused 1: Tshifhiwa Matodzi, former VBS director and chairman of the board. [Text] Accused 1: Tshifhiwa Matodzi [Text] Former VBS Director and Chairman of the board [Text] Alternative to Counts 6 to 16: Stole R2 296 599 008 (The State vs Matodzi & Others - Indictment) VO: According to the State's Indictment, Matodzi, along with Accused 2 Andile Ramavhunga Former VBS CEO, Accused 3 Philip Truter Former CFO of VBS and Accused 4 Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer of VBS created fictitious credits in the VBS accounts of companies of which they and their associates were beneficiaries. [build of first 4 accused ] In addition, allegedly on Matodzi’s instructions payments were made from VBS accounts of Matodzi entities to VBS accounts of front companies linked to all the accused. [build up to all the accused ] Whilst Matodzi was chairman of VBS he was also executive Chairman of Vele Investments which had acquired a questionable 53% shareholding in VBS. Anoosh: Vele was part and parcel of the entire scheme. So it became essentially the alter ego of the bank. Where monies were siphoned out and diverted through to Vele; Vele would then use those funds to buy up other companies and further utilize those monies for other purposes. VO: The questionable acquisition of Vele's shares in VBS forms part of Matodzi's charge sheet and is linked to the charges of Accused 7 Ernest Nesane and Accused 8 Paul Magula who were non-executive directors of VBS and represented the PIC's 26% interest in VBS Mutual Bank. [Text] Accused 7: Ernest Nesane [Text] Former PIC Executive and Non Executive Director of VBS [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others Count 38: R 7 450 000 from Accused 1 [Text] Accused 8: Paul Magula [Text] Former PIC executive [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others Count 40: R 7 000 000 from Accused 1 VO: They are both charged with defrauding the PIC for not disclosing to the PIC a VBS offer of 2 shares for every one held, Only Vele Investments took up the offer and increased its shares to 53% and the 26% PIC shareholding fell to 12 percent. Both men were allegedly paid a combined R 14.45m on Matodzi’s instruction. (beat) VO: The web of collusion started unravelling in 2018 under the curatorship of Anoosh Rooplal. In trying to save the bank, that's when he noticed irregularities in the accounting records. Anoosh: Things just weren't tying up. Essentially, when one tried to trace and understand where the assets of the bank were, you know, we found that they were really weak cases of assets and cash that were reflected on the records. VO: According to the indictment, up to February 2018, Accused 2 Andile Ramavhunga, former CEO of VBS, received illicit payments of R 23.4 million from Matodzi. [Text] Accused 2: Andile Ramavhunga [Text] Former CEO of VBS [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others Count 26: R 23 495 000 from Accused 1 VO: Accused 3: Philip Truter, former CFO of VBS is also charged with facilitating the looting of VBS. His company Shangri La Investments reportedly received over R2m in payments from Vele Investments. [Text] Accused 3: Philip Truter [Text] Former CFO of VBS [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others Count 28: R 2 250 000 from Accused 1 Plea postponed due to Covid-19 quarantine VO: Accused 4: Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer is Charged with facilitating the looting of VBS and according to the indictment Matodzi furnished him with R 17.1m. [Text] Accused 4: Phophi Mukhodobwane [Text] Former Treasurer of VBS [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others Count 30: R 17 100 000 from Accused 1 General: When you get people charged with the pattern of racketeering activities, you are not working as just an individual, it is an organized criminal group that have planned this, and they repeatedly do it. VO: Accused 5: Sipho Malaba, former KPMG partner was the External auditor responsible for signing off VBS’s fraudulent 2017 financials intended for the Reserve Bank. The charges claim payments of over R30m to Malaba’s front companies. [Text] Accused 5: Sipho Malaba [Text] Former KPMG Partner [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others Counts 32, 34: R 30 335 442 from Accused 1, 2 and 4 Anoosh: Every bank has to have third party assurance providers. The auditors are one of them. I had to withdraw those financial statements purely because they were unreliable. VO: Accused 6: Avashoni Ramikosi, former Chairman of the VBS Audit Committee and SAPS Chief Financial Officer, Was Allegedly instrumental in approving the fraudulent VBS 2017 financials. The indictment shows payments of R 750 000 to Ramikosi. [Text] Accused 6: Avashoni Ramikosi [Text] Former Chairman of the VBS Audit Committee [Text] Former SAPS Chief Financial Officer [Text] The State vs Matodzi & Others VO: Forensic Accountant Andre Prakke examined the Motau Report and the indictment and explains why he thinks the alleged looters managed to carry on for as long as they did. Andre: By the assistance of the auditor. VO: The auditor being, former KPMG partner Sipho Malaba Andre: This is a very good example where the head of the audit committee was fed information, and they knew it was not correct and it was manipulated before it went to the audit committee. It's clear from the report also that even the CFO and the directors knew things were false. The whole idea of this was to steal the money and then you forge and change and the auditor was the key person to achieve this. VO: KPMG have stated they have "fully cooperated with the Reserve Bank" … and "Any unlawful action taken by Malaba, was neither authorised nor known to KPMG". In response to our questions to all the accused, five responded. Malaba, Ramavhunga and Magula have denied any wrongdoing and intend to clear their names. Matodzi and Ramikosi are not prepared to comment at this stage. Sipho: The people that have appeared in court right now, is the chairperson of the board, is the CEO of the company and his executives. So that's where you start, and then it trickles down. You follow the money in terms of how it filters through to everybody, and that's, the the strategy of the investigation Link: Twenty municipalities were involved in this fraud, by illegally depositing a collective of 1.5 billion rand with VBS. VO: To keep this pyramid scheme alive, the accused allegedly had to solicit big investors like Municipalities, in order to have money in the bank, so they could siphon it out. Anoosh: One of the reasons that led to the curatorship was because municipalities were not legally allowed to invest the monies with the mutual bank in the first place. VO: Some municipalities did pull their money out of VBS, but others were resistant, like the Vhembe District Municipality even with mounting pressure from unions. The burning question in Vhembe today is, did some union members pay the ultimate price for their objections? Musetsho wife: It was on the 24th of January, I was cooking in the kitchen when my son come running saying mama come help daddy, and I just felt a bang, I didn't realise it’s a gun. VO: Tshililo Timson Musetsho known as TT, former Limpopo Chairperson of the South African Municipal Workers Union and Vhembe Municipality employee was gunned down at his home. The pain of losing her husband is unbearable for Luvhuenga Musetsho. Musetsho Sound up: Eish, I don't want to talk about it VO: TT's mother Agnes was with him before he passed away. Venda: Agnes: I am hurting so much, what hurts more about this VBS issue is that at the end of the day I saw him shot. He said to me Ma VBS got me, today VBS has finally got me. I am dying because of VBS. VO: Lucky Mani, describes how his brother Ronald Mani, Deputy Provincial Secretary of SAMWU, was shot at a friends shop a few days later. Lucky: There were two people that walk into the shop, and ask for the owner of the shop and then they also ask for him and from there they move around the shop and then they then shot him. VO: Both men stood against corruption in the Vhembe District Municipality which had illegally invested 300 million rand in VBS contravening the Municipal Finance Management Act. Subsequently, the Municipal Manager and the CFO were both subjected to a disciplinary process by the municipality. Pastor Dr Farisani Tshenuwani had attended a meeting involving various unions with Ronald on the day he died. Pastor: Millions were given to identified people who were willing to work with the systems some politicians in the municipalities were getting kickbacks from the monies that were being invested in the VBS. They were demanding the removal of key players in the municipalities who were promoting the rot. VO: According to the Motau report Municipal officials and middlemen were offered commissions of around 2% to deposit millions into VBS. // The Mani and Musetsho families firmly believe that the killings were linked to the VBS travesty. // A suspect in the death of Mani has been arrested. Lucky: They might have killed him, but they didn't silence his voice. VO: No arrests have yet been made in connection with TT's killing. Masa: We have two union reps who were killed and their families alleged this is because they were quite outspoken about what was going on at VBS. Sipho: We will make sure that we reveal or we extract any piece of evidence that suggests there were also other crimes that were committed like murder, connected to the VBS Bank. VO: Not even a week after the arrest of the alleged Kingpins the Hawks pounced again, this time targeting municipalities making one arrest. Link: In advocate Terry Motau's report, TheGreat Bank Heist , 53 conspirators were identified as being part of this elaborate operation, so who's next? Politicians, businessmen, corrupt municipal officials, are all implicated in Motau's report. Sipho: Anyone who has committed criminal offences with this particular matter, If I were them, I wouldn't rest. It's just a matter of time.

In early 2017, Treasury issued an instruction to municipalities to stop investing with the institution. As a result, a number of councils withdrew more than R1 billion from the bank. The victims of the shootings were Ronald Mani and Tshililo Timson Musetsho. Ronald Mani Was killed in January 2019 at his Home village in Tshisahulu outside Thohoyandou, after attending a general meeting in the Vhembe District. He was one of the few that were vocal about the looting of the bank from which over R 2,3 Billion was stolen. Their killings have been linked to the VBS looting as days before he and some of his colleagues had been addressing municipal workers about the looting. The Vhembe District Municipality had invested 311 Million into VBS Mutual Bank In contravention of the regulations. He was one of the leaders from the Union Federation Cosatu and the South african Communist party acting in various capacities at local and regional levels, until his election as deputy secretary in 2016 of the South African Municipal Workers Union. His wife is still mourning the death of her husband, particularly as no suspects, have been arrested. Her Son has said that his mother gets epileptic fits when she speaks about his death. Tshililo Timson Musetsho: Another ‘Comrade’, Tshililo Timson Musetsho, was killed before Ronald Mani. TT was rushed to the hospital where he later died. At the bail appearance of the VBS Eight Accused, Timson’s daughter wrote on twitter, “My father was brutally killed Last year because he stood up for the people and fought against VBS Looters, let you politician friend that they are also coming for them, they gonna rot in jail, my father's death will never be in vain RIP Cd TT, God is Fighting for u. # VBSArrests #VBSBankhiest. Lucky Mani, brother of Ronald Mani, has agreed to speak to Carte Blanche regarding the movement of the case. The brother of the deceased says that Ronald had been vocal long before the report was released. This intensified and they placed pressure on the municipality to stop with the illegal investments. He says that even though there is progress with the arrests of the VBS accused, nothing will make the family find solace if the killers of Mani and TT are not found. Lucky Mani says that because the death of his brother received a lot of attention in Vhembe, a group of ANC officials, union reps etc. have been helping to put pressure on the police to find the killers - It's a wait and see game for them. Case Number Sourced: 481/10/2018 Sergeant SB Libanyana Contact: 013 980 0048 South African National Civic Organisation SANCO National: SANCO: SANCO, has been representing individuals in the community most affected by the VBS Heist. They are creating a database of individuals who have lost money and are planning to demand that the government give those individuals monthly relief fund packages from the 500 Billion COVID- Relief fund, to help those who lost all their savings. NOTE: According to Mosibudi, while in Vhembe we will be able to speak to specific individuals, who lost 100k or more.: we will be able to have one or two other interviews, regarding the loss of funds through VBS and what future plans SANCO, have, to help the affected individuals.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: The Accused: Accused number 1: Tshifhiwa Matodzi, former chairman VBS The indictment shows that Matodzi had control of several accounts held at VBS Mutual Bank. The accounts included: Vele investments, Petronet, Venmont, Robvet, Khavo, Scorpion, Tiisang. These accounts controlled hundreds of millions of rand, some of which Matodzi used to bribe his co-accused, prosecutors allege. Prosecutors also accused Matodzi of offering gratification in order to influence them “to act in a manner that amounts to the illegal, dishonest, unauthorised, incomplete, or biased exercise, carrying out or performance of any powers, duties or functions arising out of a statutory, contractual or any other legal obligation”. Accused Number 2: Andile Ramavhunga, former CEO VBS Between December 2016 and February 2018, the indictment shows, Ramavhunga received about R19m into the account of “Dambale”, a company owned by him. Other accounts, held at VBS Mutual Bank, which Ramavhunga controlled, include those of Munyai Investments and another one named in the indictment as the “Ramavhunga” account. Ramavhunga received R3.7m into the Munyai Investments account. The money came from the Vele and Vele Petroport accounts, the indictment shows. Also, he received R795,000 into the Ramavhunga account from the Venmont, Vele and Petroport accounts. Up to February 2018, Ramavhunga’s accounts had received a total of R23.4m. Accused number 3: Philip Truter, former CFO VBS The indictment shows that Truter received R2m into the FNB account of a company called Shangri La Investments. Accused number 4: Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer VBS On the instruction of Matodzi, Mukhodobwane received R5.6m into the account of Lamawave Ltd. The indictment shows that a Peter Mukhodobwane, who was the sole shareholder of Lamawave, was a front for Phophi Mukhodobwane, the former treasurer. In total, Mukhodobwane received R17.1m into Lamawave and the “Mukhodobwane” accounts. Accused number 5: Sipho Malaba, former KPMG partner Malaba has been charged with fraud for signing off VBS Bank’s 2017 financial statements which gave the false impression that its finances were in a healthy state. Malaba, Matodzi, Ramavhunga, Truter, Nesane and Magula were also collectively charged with “unlawfully, falsely and with the intention to defraud ... shareholders, VBS creditors and the Registrar” approving the financial statements.” On the money trail against Malaba, the indictment shows that a company called Ihaawu Lesizwe, owned by Jacqueline Jaseman Malaba and Bafana Milundelwa Malaba, had the following accounts at VBS Mutual Bank: two vehicle finance accounts, a mortgage account and a classic business account. Betanologix, another company owned by Jacqueline Jaseman Malaba and a Mwise Mapepo, also had an account at the bank. Up to March 2018 both companies, which the indictment claims were fronts for Sipho Malaba, received up to R29.2m. Further, on Matodzi’s instruction, R654,000 was paid into the trust accounts of Makaula Zilwa Inc and NGL attorneys on behalf of Malaba. Accused number 6: Avashoni Ramikosi, former police CFO. The indictment shows that a company called Zanoware, owned by Alice Manye, was a front for Ramikosi. The company had received up to R750,000 from Venmont, one of the many accounts controlled by Matodzi. Accused number 7: Ernest Nesane, former PIC executive Nesane, the prosecutors will argue, received up to R1.1m into the account of a company called Parallel Properties owned by Rudzani Ndwammbi. Ndwammbi, prosecutors will argue, was a front for Nesane, as all monies received by Parallel Properties benefited the former PIC executive. Also, on the instruction of Matodzi, prosecutors revealed that Nesane benefited from R5.6m which was paid into Parallel Properties from the Vele account. Accused number 8: Paul Magula, former PIC executive The indictment shows that a company called Investar Connect Holdings, owned by a Lot Magosha, was a front for Magula.The company was paid R2.8m for the benefit of Magula on instruction from Matodzi.Another company, Hekima Capital, which had an account at VBS Mutual Bank, received R3.3m on behalf of Magula on Matodzi’s instruction. In addition we received an email from the family of a deceased 24 year old, Dylan Ross who was killed in a car accident on the 24th of August 2019. They allege that it was reckelss driving by Phophi Mukhodobwane, former treasurer of VBS, who fled the scene of the accident and only later report it, as well as have sms communication with the family that he felt really bad about what happened that night. They have laid a charge of reckless driving but nothing has come of the case as yet, it may be worth a one line mention... One other element which I am keen on, is that in the last 14 years only 67 municipal people have been charged with corruption of which only 9 have been convicted with sentences of 2 to 3 years and wholly suspended for 5 years. I would like the NPA to answer to; if municipal officials are charged in this case, what kind of sentences could they expect bearing in mind the nature of the crimes.
